name: Medium steel light close helm
description: A medium steel helm that closes round the whole head, with a pivoting visor over a chin guard and a low comb and one gorget plate. With the visor down you look out through a narrow slit and breathe through the slots on the right cheek.
notes: Shares batch 136's mild steel model `lc_lighthelm_close` with the plates in `steel-grey`, the medium grade; it differs only in colour, as the reference copies the mild helm. No row of its own, so the look step did not check this colouring. Slot `head`; it also covers the eyes and mouth, which the head slot is taken to include. Encumbrance and warmth follow the reference. Protection is a guess for a full steel helm graded by steel and weight, above the mild steel helm of the same pattern; the reference gives none. The xl size shares the model. Host for helmet add-ons: `helmet` points at the left side, right side and back of the rim; no front mount, because the visor covers the face and nothing that rides there could be used with it. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Spiked leather helmet
description: An old officer's helmet of hardened black leather with a peak front and back, a tall spike on a cross-shaped base, a shield-shaped plate on the front and scaled chin straps. The spike is for show.
notes: Standing on its rim, front on +z, 232 mm across, 268 mm front to back with the peaks and 244 mm tall to the spike tip: a black leather shell in `leather-black`, a front peak trimmed in metal and a deeper neck peak, a fluted spike on a round boss with four arms down the shell, a shield-shaped front plate, rosettes each side and a run of chin scales resting over the front peak. The reference gives iron fittings; they are in `brass-polished` because polished fittings are how the helmet is known and steel would not read against the trim at this grain. The id keeps the reference's word for the helmet, which is a common noun, not a brand. CHECK VOLUME (x8.7): a helmet is a hollow shell with a spike, and the reference volume counts the leather rather than the box round the head it encloses. Slot `head`; encumbrance and warmth follow the reference. Protection is a guess for hardened leather; the reference gives none. Host for helmet add-ons: `helmet` points at the left side, right side and back of the rim; no front mount, because the front plate takes the brow. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Pot helmet
description: An iron soup pot worn upside down, with a leather strap run through its side handles to buckle under the chin. Poor armour, but it still cooks.
notes: Upside down on its rim, front on +z: an iron pot 200 mm across and 130 mm deep in `iron-cast` with a rolled rim, a loop handle each side near the rim and a brown strap dropping from both handles and lying out in a loop in front with its buckle, 256 mm across with the handles. cooking 3, the pot grade, carries the reference's cooking and boiling qualities; its container and chemistry qualities are not carried over. Slot `head`; encumbrance and warmth follow the reference. Protection is a guess for a thin iron pot; the reference gives none. No `helmet` points: a pot has no rails or rim laces to take add-ons. The xs size shares the model. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Tactical full helmet
description: A charcoal-grey ballistic helmet that closes over the whole head and neck, with a moulded chin bar, a smoked visor curving round the face, black accessory rails along the sides and a mount over the brow.
notes: Standing on its neck guard, front on +z, 272 mm across and 304 mm tall: a rounded shell in `plastic-charcoal` with a chin bar and a row of black vents, a smoked visor in `lens-smoke` curving close round the shell to its pivots, with a black rim across its top, visor pivots each side, accessory rails curved along the sides behind the pivots, trim in `plastic-matte-black`, a mount shroud above the brow and a guard flaring out over the back of the neck. Tiles draw the visor opaque; it stays see-through in the game. CHECK VOLUME (x10): a helmet is a hollow shell, and the reference volume counts the shell rather than the box round the head it encloses. Slot `head`; it also covers the eyes and mouth, which the head slot is taken to include. Encumbrance and warmth follow the reference.
